reference.title: One GitHub App for the site, the editor and builds
reference.shortdesc: The exact settings of a GitHub App that signs readers and authors in, lets the web editor commit and open pull requests, and sends push webhooks for builds.

section.title: App settings

strow.stentry: Any name not yet taken on GitHub, such as Acme docs
Active; URL $PUBLIC_URL/webhooks/github; secret: the value of GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET

Contents: Read and write. Pull requests: Read and write. Administration: Read-only. Commit statuses: Read and write (the editor only reads them; builds report to them). Checks: Read-only. Metadata: Read-only.
Where can this GitHub App be installed?

section.p: After creating it, generate a client secret and a private key, install the App on the docs repository, and note the installation id from the installation's URL. Register the repository with that installationId.

section.title: A pre-filled registration link
section.p: GitHub opens the registration form pre-filled from query parameters. The repository's script prints the link for your two hosts; open it while signed in to GitHub, set the webhook secret (the one value GitHub does not take from a link), and create the App.
section.codeblock: node scripts/github-app-url.mjs https://docs.example.com https://edit.docs.example.com # for an organization's App: node scripts/github-app-url.mjs https://docs.example.com https://edit.docs.example.com "Acme docs" --org acme

strow.stentry: Recommended: refuses to share the docs host
